title_en: Hubei Wushi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Aonuo (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Wang Junshe — dispute over infringement of invention patent

full_text_en:
Hubei Wushi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Aonuo (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Wang Junshe — Dispute over Infringement of Invention Patent Right

【Ruling Summary】

When interpreting a claim, the technical content recorded in the patent specification and other claims recorded in the claims may be combined to determine the meaning of the technical terms in that claim.

Where the patentee, during the patent grant procedure, abandons a technical solution through amendments to the claims or specification or through statements of opinion, regardless of whether such amendment or statement of opinion relates to the novelty or inventiveness of the patent, such technical solution cannot be included in the scope of patent protection through the doctrine of equivalents in a dispute over infringement of a patent right.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2009) Min Ti Zi No. 20

Petitioner for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hubei Wushi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 137 Biyun Road, Anlu City, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Cheng Renzhang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hongyi, lawyer of Beijing Leader Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yongquan, lawyer of Beijing Leader Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Aonuo (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1099 Cuiyuan Street, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Hong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Hui, lawyer of Fangda Partners, Shenzhen Office.

Agent ad litem: Cao Jinyan, female, patent agent of Beijing Fanhua Weiye Intellectual Property Agency Co., Ltd., residing at Room 11, Building 7, Friendship Hotel, Haidian District, Beijing.

Defendant at First Instance: Wang Junshe, male, born on March 27, 1965, Han nationality, owner of Baoding City North District Xinkang Pharmacy, residing at No. 93 Langhu Street, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

The petitioner for retrial, Hubei Wushi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wushi Pharmaceutical Company), due to a dispute with the respondent, Aonuo (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aonuo Company), and the defendant at first instance, Wang Junshe, over infringement of an invention patent right, was dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2007) Ji Min San Zhong Zi No. 23 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court and filed a petition for retrial with this Court. On December 25, 2008, this Court rendered a Civil Ruling (2008) Min Shen Zi No. 458, granting the retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case. Agent ad litem Jiang Hongyi and Sun Xi of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company, and Agent ad litem Zhang Hui and Cao Jinyan of Aonuo Company appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The defendant at first instance, Wang Junshe, was duly summoned but failed to appear. This case is now closed.

On November 25, 2006, Aonuo Company filed a lawsuit with the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province, alleging that Aonuo Company discovered that Wushi Pharmaceutical Company was producing and extensively selling its product "Xingaitepai Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" in Hebei and elsewhere, and that Aonuo Company had purchased the allegedly infringing product at the Baoding City North District Xinkang Pharmacy operated by Wang Junshe through notarization. Aonuo Company claimed that Wushi Pharmaceutical Company and Wang Junshe had infringed its invention patent right, and requested the court to order: 1. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company and Wang Junshe to cease the production and sale of "Xingaitepai Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution"; 2. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company and Wang Junshe to publish an apology in the *China Pharmaceutical News*; 3. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company and Wang Junshe to compensate Aonuo Company for economic losses of RMB 1,941,371.44, and to bear the attorney fees and litigation costs of this case.

The Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court found the following facts at first instance: On December 5, 1995, Kong Yanping filed an application with the State Patent Office for an invention patent titled "A Medicament for Preventing or Treating Calcium Deficiency and Its Preparation Method." On December 15, 2000, the State Intellectual Property Office granted the patent right, with Patent No. ZL95117811.3, and the announcement date of authorization was January 10, 2001. Claim 1 of the patent was: "A medicament for preventing or treating calcium deficiency, characterized in that it is a medicament prepared from raw materials in the following proportions by weight: active calcium 4-8 parts, zinc gluconate 0.1-0.4 parts, glutamine or glutamic acid 0.8-1.2 parts." On April 3, 2006, the patentee Kong Yanping and Aonuo Company entered into a *Patent Exploitation License Contract*. At that time, Aonuo Company was named Aonuo Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and was later changed to Aonuo (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in the industrial and commercial registration. The contract stipulated that Kong Yanping would grant Aonuo Company an exclusive license to exploit the patent in question, with the license term equal to the patent term, without restrictions on territory or method of use. If a third party committed an act of infringement on this patent, the licensee was authorized to independently initiate an infringement lawsuit against the infringer, and the relevant legal consequences (benefits or losses) would be borne by the licensee.

On September 28, 2006, through notarization by the Second Notary Public Office of Baoding City, Aonuo Company purchased two boxes of "Xingaitepai Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" produced by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company from the Baoding City North District Xinkang Pharmacy operated by Wang Junshe. The product insert stated the ingredients as: per 10 mL containing calcium gluconate 600 mg, zinc gluconate 30 mg, and lysine hydrochloride 100 mg. The Drug Registration Approval Document from the State Food and Drug Administration (Approval No. 2005S009711) also indicated the specifications of the product as: 10 mL: calcium gluconate 0.6 g, zinc gluconate 0.03 g, and lysine hydrochloride 0.1 g.

In the published application of the patent in question, the independent claim referred to a soluble calcium agent, which included calcium gluconate, calcium chloride, calcium lactate, calcium carbonate, or active calcium. In the First Examination Opinion Notice of the State Intellectual Property Office, the examiner stated that the upper concept "soluble calcium agent" used in the claim included various soluble calcium-containing substances and covered a relatively broad scope of protection, but the applicant only provided examples of formulations using "calcium gluconate" and "active calcium" among them. For other soluble calcium agents, no formulation and effect examples were provided. A person of ordinary skill in the art could hardly foresee whether other soluble calcium agents, when formulated according to the invention, would also play the same role in the human body. The claim was essentially not supported by the description and should be amended. In response to the examiner's requirement, the applicant amended the claims, changing "soluble calcium agent" to "active calcium."

In order to determine whether the technical features of the "Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" produced by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company fell within the scope of protection of the patent right claimed by Aonuo Company, the court of first instance commissioned the Beijing Zitu Intellectual Property Appraisal Center to conduct a technical appraisal. The appraisal report issued by this institution concluded that: the product of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company contained calcium gluconate, while the patent in question involved active calcium. Active calcium and calcium gluconate are both edible calcium agents that can be absorbed by the human body; as raw materials for calcium supplements, the two are equivalent and can be chosen arbitrarily; the product of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company used lysine hydrochloride, while the patent in question used glutamine or glutamic acid. Lysine hydrochloride and the patent's glutamic acid are different amino acids with different nutritional values, but in a medicament for preventing or treating calcium deficiency, both are used in combination with calcium agents and both achieve the function and effect of promoting calcium absorption, thus the two are equivalent. Apart from the equivalence of the above features, the product of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company and the patent in question have the same use, the remaining raw materials are the same (both are zinc gluconate), and the proportions of the various raw materials are the same. The appraisal concluded: "The drug 'Xingaitepai Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution' produced by Hubei Wushi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. is equivalent to the technical solution of the patent in question."

On February 19, 2003, Aonuo Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. filed an application with the State Intellectual Property Office for an invention patent titled "An Oral Solution for Preventing or Treating Calcium Deficiency and Its Preparation Method," which was granted as Patent No. ZL03104587.1 (hereinafter referred to as the '587 patent'). Its independent claim 1 stated: "An oral solution for preventing or treating calcium deficiency, characterized in that it is a preparation made from a formulation and raw materials in the following proportions by weight: soluble calcium agent 4-9 parts, zinc gluconate 0.1-0.4 parts, lysine hydrochloride 0.8-1.2 parts." During the trial, Wushi Pharmaceutical Company argued that the accused infringing product was identical to the '587 patent, and since that patent was granted, it was inventive and was not an equivalent replacement of the patent in question.

The Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court held in its first instance judgment that: The patent right for the patent in question held by patentee Kong Yanping and the exclusive exploitation license contract entered into with Aonuo Company were lawful and valid and should be protected by law. The "Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" produced and sold by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company, as appraised by the commissioned appraisal institution, had technical features equivalent to the patent in question claimed by Aonuo Company. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company's production and sale of the above product without the permission of the patentee constituted infringement.

Only amendments or statements of opinion made by the patentee to enable the patent granting authority to determine that the patent application has novelty or inventiveness would give rise to the effect of estoppel; not all amendments or statements of opinion concerning the claims during the patent application process would lead to the application of the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel. In this case, during the patent grant procedure, the patentee amended the claims in response to the patent examiner's opinion, changing "soluble calcium agent" in the independent claim to "active calcium." This was not done to give the patent application novelty or inventiveness due to the amendment, but rather to allow the claim to be supported by the description. Therefore, this amendment does not give rise to the effect of estoppel.

As long as an accused infringing product infringes a prior patent of another person, it constitutes infringement. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company's defense that its product features were identical to the '587 patent and thus did not infringe the patent in question could not be sustained.

Aonuo Company failed to provide strong evidence for its claimed economic losses. Therefore, based on the specific circumstances of this case, including the nature of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company's infringement and the scope of sales, the court determined an appropriate amount of compensation for economic losses to be paid by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company to Aonuo Company, and additionally ordered reasonable compensation for attorney fees. Wang Junshe, as a seller, did not know that the product sold was an infringing product and had provided a legal source for the product. Aonuo Company did not dispute this. Therefore, Wang Junshe was only required to cease the infringement and was not liable for compensation. The infringing act of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company did not cause damage to Aonuo Company's reputation, so the court did not support Aonuo Company's request for an apology in a newspaper.

On March 6, 2007, the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2006) Shi Min Wu Chu Zi No. 00169: 1. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company was ordered to cease the production and sale of the "Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" product and to compensate Aonuo Company for economic losses of RMB 300,000 and attorney fees of RMB 15,000; 2. Wang Junshe was ordered to cease the sale of the "Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" product produced by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company; 3. All other claims of Aonuo Company were dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 30,015 was to be borne by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company in the amount of RMB 11,265 and by Aonuo Company in the amount of RMB 18,750. The appraisal fee of RMB 30,000 was to be borne by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company.

Wushi Pharmaceutical Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the Hebei High People's Court.

At the second instance, the Hebei High People's Court found that, aside from providing some academic articles on the concept of active calcium and the national standard for active calcium as a food, neither party submitted any other new evidence.

Wushi Pharmaceutical Company primarily used the '587 patent document as evidence to defend against Aonuo Company's claims. Therefore, on August 2, 2007, the court of second instance issued a ruling to suspend the proceedings, pending a final decision by the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Reexamination Board) on the validity of that patent. On November 13, 2006, the Patent Reexamination Board issued a *Notice of Acceptance of Request for Invalidation*, accepting the request for invalidation of the '587 patent previously filed by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company. During the trial, Wushi Pharmaceutical Company stated that it had withdrawn the request. On August 25, 2006, Hubei Furen Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. also filed a request for invalidation of the '587 patent with the Patent Reexamination Board. On September 25, 2007, Hubei Furen Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. submitted a written declaration to the Patent Reexamination Board withdrawing its request for invalidation of the '587 patent. The Patent Reexamination Board issued a *Notice of Closure of Invalidation Case* on October 11, 2007. However, on September 11, 2007, the agent of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company filed another request for invalidation of the '587 patent in his own name. On October 31, 2007, the Patent Reexamination Board issued another *Notice of Acceptance of Request for Invalidation*.

The Hebei High People's Court held at the second instance that, considering that Hubei Furen Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. had filed a request for invalidation of Aonuo Company's '587 patent and some time had passed, it intended to wait for a decision by the Patent Reexamination Board on the validity of that patent before handling this case. However, Hubei Furen Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. withdrew its request for unknown reasons. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company had also previously requested invalidation and then withdrawn the request, and now for the second time filed a request for invalidation in the name of its entrusted agent as an individual. Wushi Pharmaceutical Company could not provide a reasonable explanation for this conduct. Since the validity of the '587 patent would be favorable to its position, such repeated requests for invalidation followed by withdrawals would obviously cause unnecessary delay and a waste of administrative and judicial resources. Moreover, the "National Standard for Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" (WS1-XG-008-2001) promulgated by the State Drug Administration on March 29, 2001, had substantially the same formulation specifications as the protection scope of the claims of the '587 patent. The Document No. 404, *Notice on Publishing the Third Batch of OTC Drug Catalogs*, issued by the State Drug Administration on November 6, 2002 (Guo Yao Jian An [2002] No. 404), included the formulation proportions of "Calcium Gluconate and Zinc Gluconate Oral Solution" in its appendix *Third Batch of OTC Drug Catalog (2)*, which was also substantially identical to the technical solution of the '587 patent. It was evidently improper for the State Intellectual Property Office to grant the patent after the national standards and related documents had been promulgated.

The court of first instance, when commissioning a professional institution to conduct a technical appraisal *ex officio*, did not notify the parties, which was inappropriate, but this did not constitute a procedural violation in the appraisal. Therefore, the appraisal report could still be used as the basis for deciding this case. The request of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company for a new appraisal or supplementary appraisal was dismissed. The amendment to the claims by the applicant of the patent in question was only made to allow the claims to be supported by the description, not to confer novelty or inventiveness on the patent application as a result of the amendment. Therefore, this amendment did not give rise to the effect of estoppel. The specification of the patent in question provided examples of formulations using "calcium gluconate." It was obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art that "calcium gluconate" and "active calcium," when formulated according to the invention, would play the same role in the human body, indicating that there is no substantial difference between active calcium and calcium gluconate as raw materials for the preparation of calcium supplement drugs, and the two can be equivalently replaced. According to the attachment to the Document No. 131, *Notice on Publishing the Results of the Re-evaluation of Local Standard Varieties of Respiratory System Drugs and Vitamins and Minerals*, issued by the State Drug Administration on April 10, 2000 (Guo Yao Guan An [2000] No. 131), it was directly stated that for "Xingaitet Oral Liquid" (Aonuo Company's product), "lysine hydrochloride 10g may be used to replace glutamic acid 10g." Moreover, the appraisal conclusion made by the professional institution commissioned by the court of first instance also found that "active calcium" and "calcium gluconate," and "glutamic acid or glutamine" and "lysine hydrochloride" were each equivalent. Therefore, the product produced by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company fell within the scope of protection of the patent right exclusively licensed to Aonuo Company, constituting infringement.

On December 17, 2007, the Hebei High People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2007) Ji Min San Zhong Zi No. 23: dismissing the appeal and affirming the first instance judgment. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 30,015 was to be borne by Wushi Pharmaceutical Company.

Wushi Pharmaceutical Company, in its petition for retrial, alleged: 1. Claim 1 of the patent in question, as a closed composition claim, had defined in a closed manner the types and scope of components it contained, while the accused infringing product contained multiple other components beyond the closed scope of Claim 1, which was sufficient to prove that the accused infringing product did not fall within the scope of protection of Claim 1 of the patent in question. 2. During the examination process of the patent in question, the patentee deleted the technical solution using calcium gluconate as the calcium component from the published claims. This act gave rise to the legal consequence of estoppel with respect to the patent in question. The first and second instance judgments, which found that the accused infringing product using calcium gluconate as the calcium component fell within the scope of protection of Claim 1 of the patent in question, clearly violated the doctrine of estoppel. 3. Since the "active calcium" component defined in Claim 1 of the patent in question and the "calcium gluconate" component used in the accused infringing product have diametrically opposite water-soluble physical properties, there is an essential difference between the two as raw materials for the preparation of oral solution drugs using water as the dissolution medium, and they are by no means technical means that can be equivalently replaced. 4. During the process of applying for the '587 patent, the respondent demonstrated through comparative tests that the "lysine hydrochloride" component used in the accused infringing product, when used as a raw material for the preparation of calcium supplement drugs, has significant differences in technical effect compared to the "glutamine or glutamic acid" component defined in Claim 1 of the patent in question. Therefore, whether from the perspective of respecting objective facts or from the perspective of preventing the respondent from going back on its word to reflect the principle of fairness and reasonableness, the two components should not be found equivalent in this case.

Aonuo Company argued in response: 1. Claim 1 of the patent in question is not a closed expression, and regardless of whether it is a closed expression, the accused infringing product falls within its scope of protection. 2. During the examination process of the patent in question, the amendment was not made with respect to novelty or inventiveness, nor was any content explicitly abandoned or deleted. The patentee's amendment from "soluble calcium agent" to "active calcium" was a clarifying amendment. The amended "active calcium" refers to calcium in ionic form, also known as calcium ion, which includes all component calcium, including calcium gluconate. This amendment does not trigger the application of the doctrine of estoppel. 3. Aonuo Company does not deny that "lysine hydrochloride can significantly increase the solubility and physicochemical stability of calcium gluconate relative to glutamine or glutamic acid." However, the '587 patent is a selection invention based on the patent in question, and the two are inclusive. Infringement of the '587 patent necessarily infringes the patent in question.

Upon review, this Court confirms that the facts found by the courts of first and second instance are true.

In the retrial, this Court considers that the main issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Whether Claim 1 is a closed structure and how to interpret "active calcium" recorded in Claim 1; (2) Whether active calcium and calcium gluconate are equivalent; (3) Whether glutamine or glutamic acid and lysine hydrochloride are equivalent.

1.  Regarding whether Claim 1 is a closed structure and how to interpret the "active calcium" described in Claim 1.  Patent Claim 1 is a composition claim, using the expression "a medicament prepared from the raw materials in the following weight ratios."  This expression in Claim 1 does not fall within the forms of closed expressions such as "consisting of" or "composed of" as enumerated in Section 4.2.1, Chapter 10, Part II of the "Examination Guidelines" (2006 edition) formulated by the State Intellectual Property Office.  Furthermore, from the limiting relationship between Claim 1 and Claim 2, Claim 1 is not a closed expression.  Claim 2, which is dependent on Claim 1, defines the medicament as a powder or oral liquid.  Generally, a dependent claim is a further limitation on the independent claim, not an expansion.  Where dependent Claim 2 further defines that the medicament in Claim 1 can be a powder or oral liquid, it is evident that Claim 2 also includes components other than active calcium, zinc gluconate, and glutamine or glutamic acid, indicating that Claim 1 may include components other than active calcium, zinc gluconate, and glutamine or glutamic acid.  Therefore, Claim 1 should be construed as a claim in an open-ended expression.

Regarding whether the "active calcium" described in Claim 1 includes "calcium gluconate."  Claim 2 of the published patent application and page 2 of the description clearly state that soluble calcium agents are "calcium gluconate, calcium chloride, calcium lactate, calcium carbonate, or active calcium."  It can be seen that in the published patent application, calcium gluconate and active calcium are two parallel types of soluble calcium agents; calcium gluconate is not a type of active calcium.  Additionally, Example 1 of the description of the published patent application records a technical solution using calcium gluconate as a raw material, while Example 2 records a technical solution using active calcium as a raw material, further illustrating that calcium gluconate and active calcium are specific parallel calcium raw materials, and calcium gluconate is not a type of active calcium.  Aonuo Company argues that the patent applicant's amendment of "soluble calcium agents" to "active calcium" during the examination process of the patent-in-suit was a clarifying amendment, and that the amended term "active calcium" includes all calcium components, including calcium gluconate.  However, it can be seen from the examination file of the patent-in-suit that the patent applicant made the above amendment in response to the examination opinion of the State Intellectual Property Office that the scope of protection of "soluble calcium agents" in the claims of the published patent application was too broad and was not substantially supported by the description.  At the same time, the patent applicant did not state in the opinion statement at the time of amendment that active calcium included calcium gluconate.  Therefore, the respondent's assertion that active calcium in the patent-in-suit includes calcium gluconate cannot be established.

2.  Regarding whether active calcium and calcium gluconate are equivalent.  As elaborated in issue (1) above on whether "active calcium" includes "calcium gluconate," the patentee, during the patent grant procedure, made amendments to Claim 1, thereby abandoning the technical solution incorporating the technical feature of "calcium gluconate."  According to the principle of estoppel, a technical solution abandoned by a patent applicant or patentee through amendments to the claims or description or through opinion statements during the patent grant or invalidation proceedings cannot be included within the scope of patent protection in patent infringement disputes.  Therefore, the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit should not include the technical solution containing the technical feature "calcium gluconate."  The corresponding technical feature of the accused infringing product is calcium gluconate, which is a technical solution abandoned by the patentee during the patent grant procedure.  It should not be considered equivalent to the "active calcium" technical feature described in Claim 1 and thereby included within the patent's scope of protection.  The original trial judgment misunderstood the principle of estoppel and improperly found the two features to be equivalent.

3.  Regarding whether glutamine or glutamic acid and L-lysine hydrochloride are equivalent.  In the "Opinion Statement" submitted by the patentee of Patent No. 587 during its examination process, it was stated that adding L-lysine hydrochloride to a zinc gluconate solution, compared to formulations adding glutamine or glutamic acid, produced unexpected effects in the physicochemical properties of the calcium gluconate oral liquid, with significant improvements in the solubility and stability of calcium gluconate, and corresponding experimental data were provided to support this assertion.  The State Intellectual Property Office also granted Patent No. 587 based on this argument.  Since the main difference between Claim 1 of Patent No. 587 and Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit is the replacement of "glutamic acid or glutamine" as stated in Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit with "L-lysine hydrochloride," it can be seen that, in the sense of patent law, there is a substantive difference between the technical features "glutamic acid or glutamine" and "L-lysine hydrochloride" concerning the manufacture of a zinc gluconate solution.  The corresponding technical feature of the accused infringing product is L-lysine hydrochloride.  Compared with the technical feature of "glutamic acid or glutamine" as stated in Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, the two should not be considered equivalent technical features.  Although the attachment to the "Notice" of the State Drug Administration, Guo Yao Guan An [2000] No. 131, announced that "10g of L-lysine hydrochloride could be used to replace 10g of glutamic acid," this is merely an administrative management measure adopted by the State and does not constitute an equivalent substitution in the sense of patent law.  Therefore, it cannot be concluded that the L-lysine hydrochloride technical feature of the accused infringing product is equivalent to the "glutamic acid or glutamine" technical feature described in Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit.

In view of the fact that the two technical features of the accused infringing product, "calcium gluconate" and "L-lysine hydrochloride," are neither identical nor equivalent to the corresponding technical features "active calcium" and "glutamic acid or glutamine" described in Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, the accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of patent protection.  Therefore, the acts of Wushi Pharmaceutical Company and Wang Junshe in manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product do not constitute patent infringement.  The original trial judgment applied the law incorrectly and the judgment was erroneous, and should be corrected.  The main grounds for retrial asserted by the applicant for retrial are established and should be supported.  Pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1.  The Civil Judgment (2006) Shi Min Wu Chu Zi No. 00169 of the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court, Hebei Province, and the Civil Judgment (2007) Ji Min San Zhong Zi No. 23 of the Hebei High People's Court are hereby reversed.

2.  The claims of Aonuo (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. are hereby dismissed.

The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 60,030, and the technical appraisal fee of RMB 30,000, shall be borne by Aonuo (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang
